name: SEOKart
summary: Shopify and BigCommerce SEO app with one-click AI optimisation: bulk meta tags, image alt text and file names, URL edits, JSON-LD schema and rich snippets, 404 fixing and 301 redirects, image compression for page speed, and a built-in keyword rank tracker with a Cruise Control auto-SEO mode.
best_for: Shopify or BigCommerce merchants with a few hundred to a few thousand products who want on-page SEO cleaned up in bulk: meta tags, image alt text and file names, URLs, JSON-LD schema, 404s and redirects, image compression for page speed, and who would rather have a keyword rank tracker in the same app than pay for a second subscription
skip_if: you need keyword research, backlink data or content strategy, none of which this does; or you want daily rank checks, because the tracker runs monthly on Free and weekly above it. A small catalogue is not a reason to skip the app: if the free plan's 50 pages already cover you, the answer is to stay on Free, which the vendor says has no time limit
honest_knock: Every plan, free included, lists free SEO consultancy, and it is worth knowing what sits next to it. seokart.com sells a managed SEO service at $799, $1,299 and $1,949 a month (read 14 September 2026). That is a separate, optional service rather than a tier of the app, and a free consultation is the natural place for a conversation about it to start. The evidence base is decent rather than deep: 69 reviews on 12 September 2026, launched 4 June 2020, developer Activant Solutions Pvt Ltd in Jaipur. The average hides the shape: 67 five-star reviews and two one-star, with nothing in between. Then the two limits that decide whether this is the right tool. The rank tracker checks monthly on Free and weekly on Pro and above, so it is a trend line, not a daily rank check, and 100 tracked keywords is what every Shopify plan card publishes, but that is not the ceiling: the vendor's own configurator at seokart.com/pricing sells 200 to 500 tracked keywords as a priced step, $10 a month per extra 100 on a 1,000-product store and $20 a step on a 10,000-product one (read 15 September 2026). And one-click AI optimisation writes meta titles and descriptions in bulk: that is the whole appeal. This review is researched rather than hands-on, so take the next line as general practice with any bulk AI writer and not as something we watched SEOKart produce -- budget a pass for reading what it wrote on your best-selling pages before you let Cruise Control run unattended. The app also needs access to products, store analytics and the Online Store, plus blog contributor data.

pricing.notes:
(price read 2026-09-12, re-verified 2026-09-15 and again unchanged on 2026-10-14) Two publishers, and they do not publish the same ladder. The Shopify listing, https://apps.shopify.com/seokart, bills in USD and recurs every 30 days through Shopify, with four fixed tiers. Free covers 50 pages of one-click AI optimisation, 10 tracked keywords checked monthly, 50 image optimisations and 50 pages of bulk editing, with limited rich snippets. Pro is $20 a month or $216 a year for 1,000 products with 100 tracked keywords checked weekly, unlimited image and bulk optimisation, full rich snippets, a 404 fixer and Cruise Control auto-SEO. Plus is $30 a month or $324 a year for 5,000 products, Max $40 or $432 for 10,000, and annual billing saves 10% on all three. On those four cards the tracked-keyword line never moves off 100 and the feature lists above Pro are word for word identical.

The vendor's own page sells the same app as one configurable Pro plan and runs much further. Under the APP tab on https://seokart.com/pricing (read 15 September 2026) the card carries two dropdowns. Catalogue size, priced at the base 100 keywords: 1,000 products $20 a month, 5,000 $30, 10,000 $40, 25,000 $75, 50,000 $100, 100,000 $150, 500,000 $300, 1,000,000 $500 and 2,000,000 $800. Tracked keywords are the second dropdown and run 100, 200, 300, 400, 500. That step is charged, and it costs more the larger the catalogue: on 1,000 products the five choices are $20, $30, $40, $50 and $60 a month, and on 10,000 products they are $40, $60, $80, $100 and $120. So 500 keywords on a 10,000-product store is $120 a month, three times the $40 the Shopify card presents as the top of the range. The first three catalogue rungs match the Shopify tiers exactly; what the listing leaves out is everything above 10,000 products and the keyword dropdown altogether.

The same vendor page also sells a managed SEO service at $799, $1,299 and $1,949 a month (read 14 September 2026). That is a separate, optional service alongside the app, and it is what the free SEO consultancy in the plan table opens the door to. The app is sold for BigCommerce too: that listing, https://www.bigcommerce.com/apps/seokart/ (read 14 September 2026, last updated there 2 September 2026), publishes a $20 a month recurring fee, no upfront charge and a 10-day free trial.

compare_with.name: StoreSEO
compare_with.why: Both bulk-optimise a Shopify store's metadata, and the split is catalogue size against the free ceiling. StoreSEO's Free Forever covers 25 products and its first paid tier, Lite, is $14.99 a month for 100 (read 19 August 2026); SEOKart's free tier covers 50 pages of AI optimisation and its first paid tier is $20 a month for 1,000 products with 100 tracked keywords. Under a hundred products StoreSEO is the cheaper way in. Above that the comparison flips, because $20 covering a thousand products is the cheapest full-catalogue step of the two, and rank tracking is included rather than bought separately

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested SEOKart on a Shopify development store: the install, the automatic audit, one AI written meta description (discarded), the plan screen, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (not approved), the Free plan and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved. Install: the App Store listing (English) is SEOKart; the install screen asked for View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (products, store analytics, Online Store). Install was clicked at about 12:27; no vendor account, phone number or call was asked. The app opened straight on the SEO Dashboard on the Free plan without any payment screen; a chat pop-up and a product tour came first and were both closed. Core action: the audit started by itself at install. After about 40 seconds (12:28) the dashboard said 28 / 28 pages audited with a score of 63% and We found 26 errors: Meta 24, Content 2, Image 0, Broken 0; it also showed Empty Meta Description 8 and Total Products 19. At 12:30 Fix Errors led to SEO Optimizer AI; for the product Appointment (60%) one click on Run AI Optimization filled a Target Keyword (Book Appointment Online) and a Meta Description of 107 characters that mentions our store name. The app then still said 4 Issues, and its own check asks for 120 to 160 characters. The bar Unsaved changes with Discard and Save appeared; we pressed Discard, so nothing was saved and the shop was not changed. The separate link Run AI Assist next to the description did nothing on two clicks. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 1 minute from the start of the install to the audit result, and about 3 minutes to the first AI text, in about 5 clicks (Fix Errors, skip the tour, Run AI Optimization). Plans: Change Plan opened SEO App & Managed Services Plans with tabs App and SEO Services and a Monthly or Yearly switch. Free $0 a month: up to 50 products, 10 keywords with a monthly check, 5 prompts in the Visibility Tracker, 50 pages and 50 AI credits. Pro $20 a month: 1,000 products, 100 keywords with a weekly check, 10 prompts weekly and 200 AI credits. Pro AI $45 a month, marked New: 25 prompts and Unlimited AI Credits. We saw no Plus or Max card with $30 or $40; the product dropdown was not opened. The Pro AI plan and the Visibility Tracker are not in the dossier. Checkout: Pro and Confirm Payment (US$20.00 / month) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: SEOKart, $20,00 USD every 30 days, subtotal $20,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total Due 17 Nov $20,00 and an Add payment method row. There was no trial line and no sentence about a test charge, and Approve was greyed out, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. The Free plan stayed active. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, SEOKart and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Select all that apply); we chose Testing multiple apps. Not tested: saving a change, the Bulk Optimizer, the Image Optimizer, the 404 Fixer, Cruise Control, the rank tracker, Report and Restore, Pro and Pro AI (a payment method was needed), BigCommerce, the SEO Services tab and the Schedule a Call banner. Clean up: at about 12:32 the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps and it is gone from the installed apps. No theme change was made and nothing was saved. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The AI written meta description was 107 characters and the app itself still showed 4 issues and wants 120 to 160 characters, the link Run AI Assist did nothing on two clicks, the Pro AI plan is not in the dossier and the Pro approval screen needs a payment method.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested SEOKart on a Shopify development store: the install, the automatic audit, one AI written meta description (discarded), the plan screen, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (not approved), the Free plan and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved. Install: the App Store listing (English) is SEOKart; the install screen asked for View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (products, store analytics, Online Store). Install was clicked at about 12:27; no vendor account, phone number or call was asked. The app opened straight on the SEO Dashboard on the Free plan without any payment screen; a chat pop-up and a product tour came first and were both closed. Core action: the audit started by itself at install. After about 40 seconds (12:28) the dashboard said 28 / 28 pages audited with a score of 63% and We found 26 errors: Meta 24, Content 2, Image 0, Broken 0; it also showed Empty Meta Description 8 and Total Products 19. At 12:30 Fix Errors led to SEO Optimizer AI; for the product Appointment (60%) one click on Run AI Optimization filled a Target Keyword (Book Appointment Online) and a Meta Description of 107 characters that mentions our store name. The app then still said 4 Issues, and its own check asks for 120 to 160 characters. The bar Unsaved changes with Discard and Save appeared; we pressed Discard, so nothing was saved and the shop was not changed. The separate link Run AI Assist next to the description did nothing on two clicks. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 1 minute from the start of the install to the audit result, and about 3 minutes to the first AI text, in about 5 clicks (Fix Errors, skip the tour, Run AI Optimization). Plans: Change Plan opened SEO App & Managed Services Plans with tabs App and SEO Services and a Monthly or Yearly switch. Free $0 a month: up to 50 products, 10 keywords with a monthly check, 5 prompts in the Visibility Tracker, 50 pages and 50 AI credits. Pro $20 a month: 1,000 products, 100 keywords with a weekly check, 10 prompts weekly and 200 AI credits. Pro AI $45 a month, marked New: 25 prompts and Unlimited AI Credits. We saw no Plus or Max card with $30 or $40; the product dropdown was not opened. The Pro AI plan and the Visibility Tracker are not in the dossier. Checkout: Pro and Confirm Payment (US$20.00 / month) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: SEOKart, $20,00 USD every 30 days, subtotal $20,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total Due 17 Nov $20,00 and an Add payment method row. There was no trial line and no sentence about a test charge, and Approve was greyed out, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. The Free plan stayed active. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, SEOKart and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Select all that apply); we chose Testing multiple apps. Not tested: saving a change, the Bulk Optimizer, the Image Optimizer, the 404 Fixer, Cruise Control, the rank tracker, Report and Restore, Pro and Pro AI (a payment method was needed), BigCommerce, the SEO Services tab and the Schedule a Call banner. Clean up: at about 12:32 the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps and it is gone from the installed apps. No theme change was made and nothing was saved. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The AI written meta description was 107 characters and the app itself still showed 4 issues and wants 120 to 160 characters, the link Run AI Assist did nothing on two clicks, the Pro AI plan is not in the dossier and the Pro approval screen needs a payment method.
